source_name: ProCredit Bank Ukraine — Тендери / cooperation-proposal form
why_relevant: German-owned private bank publishing its four supplier-selection principles (відкритість, рівноправ'я, економічність, відповідальність) and a 'Пропозиції співпраці' intake form. Note the tender archive is stale (latest entries dated 2008), so treat it as an onboarding channel rather than a demand feed — a useful calibration case for how misleading a bank tender page can be.

source_name: Clarity Project — counterparty profile, AT KREDI AGRIKOL BANK (EDRPOU 14361575)
why_relevant: Analytics aggregator over Prozorro and registry data, profiling banks by EDRPOU with counts and values of procurement participation and signed contracts. For private banks it captures the sliver of activity that does touch the public system (banking services sold to state buyers, and occasional buy-side appearances), plus corporate registry linkage useful for identifying affiliated procurement entities.

source_name: Bank Pivdenny — audit-firm selection competition announcement
why_relevant: Pivdenny publishes no general procurement section, but does announce statutory selection competitions — a mandatory-audit-firm competition dated 14.08.2026 was observed via search. Regulatory obligation (audit firm selection) is therefore the one reliable forced-disclosure channel for this bank. Note the bank's live domain is bank.com.ua, not pivdenny.ua.

source_name: Universal Bank / monobank — corporate site (no procurement channel observed)
why_relevant: Registered as a low-yield watch target rather than a working source. No supplier-registration, tender or procurement-policy page was located for Universal Bank or the monobank project despite targeted uk-language searching. Worth periodic re-check because monobank's rapid IT scaling implies substantial vendor spend that is currently wholly invisible.

source_name: EBRD Client e-Procurement Portal (ECEPP) — notices
why_relevant: Since 2019 ECEPP is the ONLY place EBRD clients publish General Procurement Notices, prequalification, shortlisting and contract-award notices for EBRD-financed public-sector contracts. Ukraine notices found in search (e.g. 'Ukraine: Procurement Practices Reform', 'Ukraine: PIS Consultant and FIDIC Engineer') confirm live UA flow. Notices name the implementing entity, budget and technology scope, typically months before any national tender.

source_name: EBRD Procurement Notices hub (ebrd.com)
why_relevant: Official pointer page explaining that project procurement notices moved to ECEPP, plus rules, eligibility and links to corporate/TC consultancy streams. Useful for understanding notice taxonomy (GPN, SPN, invitation for tenders, contract award) needed to parse ECEPP correctly.

source_name: EBRD consultancy/technical-cooperation assignment notices (ECEPP consultancy stream)
why_relevant: TC/consultancy assignments are where financial-sector modernisation appears earliest (bank IT diagnostics, payment system advisory, digital banking roadmaps for UA partner banks). These precede any hardware/software tender.

source_name: World Bank Projects & Operations — Procurement notices / Current Opportunities
why_relevant: Publishes General Procurement Notices, Specific Procurement Notices, REOI for consultants and contract award notices for WB-financed operations, filterable by country. Ukraine has a large WB operational portfolio (PEACE, sectoral projects) touching public financial management and digital delivery.

source_name: World Bank Documents & Reports — Ukraine Procurement Plans (STEP-derived)
why_relevant: Project Procurement Plans list every planned contract, package description, estimated cost, method and expected dates — the single richest forward-looking artefact in the WB pipeline. Confirmed Ukraine examples retrieved in search (P508490, P1710501).

source_name: World Bank Corporate Procurement — contract awards
why_relevant: Awards of WB's own corporate contracts (>US$100k), including advisory and payment-service-provider engagements. Indirect for UA but reveals which vendors WBG trusts for payments work, occasionally Ukraine-scoped.

source_name: IFC — Ukraine country page and advisory/investment disclosures
why_relevant: IFC works through partner banks rather than public tenders (US$2bn Ukraine package; digital infrastructure among priority areas). Its disclosed investment/advisory summaries name the Ukrainian bank counterpart and the digital/payments scope, which later becomes that bank's own procurement.

source_name: EIB project procurement pages + Guide to Procurement
why_relevant: EIB does not run a central notice board for promoter-led tenders; it points to promoter publication (in UA increasingly Prozorro) and to TED for EU-rules contracts. Essential for knowing WHERE EIB-financed UA notices actually surface. EIB Ukraine portfolio via Prozorro reported at ~US$981m in lots.

source_name: UNDP Procurement Notices portal (procurement-notices.undp.org)
why_relevant: UNDP Ukraine is one of the largest donor implementers in UA and publishes ITB/RFP/RFI notices with reference prefix UNDP-UKR-*. Confirmed live UA notices including IT/office equipment RFI (UNDP-UKR-01559) and HRMIS RFP. Directly relevant to hardware, IT systems and digital-government/payments adjacent buys.

source_name: UNDP Ukraine country office procurement page
why_relevant: Country-office pointer listing active UA solicitations and contact points (e.g. procurement.dg.ua@undp.org for democratic-governance/digital projects), plus local rules and vendor onboarding.

source_name: United Nations Global Marketplace (UNGM) — tender notices
why_relevant: Single aggregation point for 40+ UN entities' tenders and, for many, contract awards; filterable by beneficiary country Ukraine. Captures agencies that have no visible standalone board (IOM, UNICEF, WFP, UNHCR, FAO) buying IT/financial-service items in UA.

source_name: UNOPS eSourcing
why_relevant: UNOPS is a major infrastructure/equipment implementer in Ukraine; its competitions run on eSourcing (vendor account via UNGM required). Relevant for equipment and systems packages under donor-funded reconstruction.

source_name: Prozorro donor-procedure channel for IFI/donor-funded purchases (Prozorro Infobox)
why_relevant: CEB, EBRD, EIB and the World Bank agreed a harmonised approach allowing Prozorro to host small IFI-financed tenders (thresholds reported around EUR 130k goods/services, EUR 5m works). This means a growing share of donor-financed UA financial-infrastructure buys is visible in Prozorro rather than only on lender portals — a critical routing fact for this cell.

source_name: Ministry of Economy of Ukraine — donor procurement rule announcements
why_relevant: Official confirmations of which donors have approved Prozorro use and under which constructor-based donor procedure; also announces which ministries will channel donor money through Prozorro. Determines where to look for a given lender's UA notices.

source_name: EU Funding & Tenders Portal — Ukraine opportunities
why_relevant: Central publication point for EU-funded calls and tenders open to/for Ukraine, including Ukraine Facility and Ukraine Investment Framework instruments that channel money to IFIs and Ukrainian banks as intermediaries — the upstream of many financial-sector procurements.

source_name: TED (Tenders Electronic Daily) — EU external-action and EU Delegation to Ukraine notices
source_subtype: official EU tender journal / open data
why_relevant: Publishes EU external-action service contracts including those of the EU Delegation to Ukraine and EU-financed technical assistance; also carries EIB-related notices under EU rules. Has bulk open data and a documented search API — the most machine-friendly source in this cell.

source_name: EU4Business Ukraine (eu4business.org.ua) — calls and project registry
why_relevant: Publishes EU4Business grant calls and a registry of 40+ SME-support projects in Ukraine, including an 'access to finance' cluster implemented through Ukrainian partner banks. Names the bank intermediaries and instrument scope — leading indicator of bank-side systems spend.

source_name: EEAS / EU Delegation to Ukraine — calls and tender announcements
why_relevant: The Delegation publishes its own calls for tenders and calls for proposals (confirmed examples: EU4Business micro-grant call; Delegation security-services tender). Also announces bank-channelled instruments (e.g. support via Bank Lviv), naming Ukrainian financial institutions.

source_name: SAM.gov — US federal contract and assistance opportunities (post-USAID State Dept. successor programming)
why_relevant: After USAID's closure the State Department absorbed continuing Ukraine assistance, including oversight of direct budget support. Any successor solicitations, NOFOs and awards for Ukraine economic/financial-sector programming must be posted on SAM.gov. Also exposes prime implementers who then subcontract in UA.

source_name: USAID Office of Inspector General — Ukraine assistance audits
why_relevant: Audits of direct budget support and Ukraine programmes disclose disbursement mechanics, implementing partners and financial-channel arrangements (e.g. the 2026 audit of direct budget support to Ukraine) that are not visible in tender notices themselves.
